management.text: Total Thyroidectomy
Total thyroidectomy ± central compartment neck dissection (level VI) for confirmed malignancy.
Intraoperative RLN monitoring. Post-op: levothyroxine replacement (lifelong). Monitor calcium × 24 h — oral calcium if symptomatic hypocalcaemia.
[surgical] Large / expanding haematoma: return to theatre — evacuate clot, achieve haemostasis, re-close or VAC.
[surgical] Cervical haematoma with airway compromise: immediate wound opening at bedside (undo sutures + skin clips), secure airway, emergency re-operation.
[followup] Review anticoagulation plan with haematology / cardiology post-event; wound review at 2 weeks.

Investigation: FBC, coagulation screen (identify coagulopathy) (urgent)

Protamine sulfate 1 mg per 100 units heparin given in last 4 h IV (intravenous) slow injection Single dose over 10 min — Heparin reversal — calculate dose based on heparin given in last 4 h
Vitamin K (phytomenadione) 10 mg IV (intravenous) slow injection Single dose (onset 6 h) — Warfarin reversal
Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP) 15 mL/kg IV (intravenous) infusion Single infusion — repeat if INR not corrected — Warfarin reversal bridge while vitamin K takes effect
Idarucizumab (Praxbind) 5 g IV (intravenous) Two doses of 2.5 g IV over 5–10 min each — Dabigatran reversal
Andexanet alfa (Ondexxya) Per weight/dose protocol — IV bolus then infusion IV (intravenous) Single treatment course — Rivaroxaban / apixaban reversal — if available
Tranexamic acid 1 g IV (intravenous) Single dose (can repeat at 8 h if ongoing haemorrhage) — Haemostasis promotion for expanding haematoma
Paracetamol 1 g PO / IV (oral or intravenous) QDS (four times daily) — Analgesia — avoid NSAIDs (antiplatelet effect)

management.text: • Arrange CT abdomen/pelvis — pancreatic protocol (triple-phase contrast).
• MRCP — biliary tree anatomy and level of obstruction.
• Discuss ERCP biliary stenting — jaundice palliation if indicated.
• Refer HPB oncology — staging and multidisciplinary team discussion.
• 2 × large-bore IV cannulae, Hartmann's 500ml bolus, crossmatch 2 units pRBC.
• Urgent OGD / colonoscopy — within 24h of haemodynamic stabilisation.
• Reverse anticoagulation if on warfarin/DOAC — Vitamin K IV + 4-factor PCC if life-threatening.
• USS abdomen — biliary tree, gallstones, hepatic parenchyma.
• 12-lead ECG — pre-operative cardiac baseline (age ≥ 40).
• 12-lead ECG — arrhythmia, right heart strain pattern (PE).
• CTPA if Wells score ≥ 2 — exclude pulmonary embolism.
• IV fluid challenge 500ml if hypovolaemia likely — reassess HR at 30 min.
• Urine protein:creatinine ratio — nephrotic syndrome (PCR > 300mg/mmol).
• Dietitian referral — pre-operative nutritional support. Delay elective surgery ≥ 4 weeks if possible.
• Prescribe ONS (Ensure/Fortisip) ×2 — pre-op nutritional optimisation (ERAS).
• If albumin < 25 g/L and surgery urgent: parenteral nutrition pre-operatively with nutrition team support.
• Calculate FIB-4 score — non-invasive fibrosis assessment (cirrhosis risk).
• Confirm cervical smear date — document last result.
• Refer gynaecology — cervical smear overdue (> 3 years).
• Document last mammogram date — refer to radiology if overdue.
• Arrange bilateral mammogram — screening protocol.
